facts.claim: Chiang et al. (2024) describe Chatbot Arena, now LMArena: people put one question to two anonymous models and vote for the better reply, and the votes become a ranking. It had over 240,000 votes when the paper came out.
Singh et al. (2025) found some providers test many private versions on Chatbot Arena and publish only the best; Meta tested 27 before Llama 4’s release.
Zhang et al. (2024) wrote GSM1k, fresh maths questions like a popular public test, and some models scored up to 8 points lower on it: they had partly learned the public test itself.
Anthropic’s price list (checked October 2026) charges per million tokens, input and output priced apart; output costs five times input, e.g. $2 in and $10 out for Claude Sonnet 5.5.
NVIDIA’s benchmarking guide (checked October 2026) defines time to first token as the wait from sending a request to the first token back, and end-to-end latency as the wait for the whole reply.
Anthropic’s deprecations page (checked October 2026) promises at least 60 days’ notice before retiring a public model, and advises testing the replacement well before that date.
OpenAI’s prompt engineering guide (checked October 2026) advises pinning production apps to a model snapshot and building evals that measure behaviour across versions.
